lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The code URL looks like a placeholder; use a working, professional link.
Consider adding a LinkedIn profile if relevant.
Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not needed for most applications and can invite irrelevant screening bias.

items.says: Use a consistent city-and-country format across entries.
Define what diagnostic accuracy measures and give the comparison baseline.
items.because: The 35% result is hard to interpret without them.

items.says: Say whether the 35% increase is relative or in percentage points.
Give brief context for what was validated in the tool-use trajectories.
items.because: Readers need to understand what was validated.

items.says: Clarify what “in-scope signals” means.
Explain how reviewer disagreement was calculated.
Say whether the change from 14% to 6% is in percentage points or a relative reduction.
Explain how “equal accuracy” was established.
items.because: The evaluation set or comparison would give the result context.

items.says: Use spelling consistent with the rest of the résumé instead of “penalises.”
items.because: That British spelling differs from the résumé’s otherwise US locations and conventions.

items.says: Clarify what “citation quality” measures or name the evaluation criteria.
Show why catching two regressions mattered, if possible.
items.because: The impact currently stops at detection.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking method repeats the diagnostic-accuracy bullet.
items.because: Repeating the same work makes the résumé look padded and obscures distinct contributions.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the diagnostics triage branch.
Explain how the backlog reduction was measured or attributed to the launch.
Make clear what the system does with the 800+ sensor signals.
items.because: The detail is useful if it shows scale.

items.says: Specify what the 4× GPU-memory reduction refers to.
Say whether the change affected model quality or training capacity, if relevant.
Verify or clarify the description “FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.”
items.because: It may be technically unclear.

items.says: Clarify the load-test conditions or traffic level if they affect the latency figures.
items.because: That context may materially affect the 420 ms and 180 ms results.

items.says: Make clear that the 200 ms build threshold applies after the optimization.
“Maintained” and “adds” switch between past and present tense.
Clarify what “release cycles to 3 days” measures.
Explain how the automated checks contributed to the shorter release cycles.
Quantify the dispatch delays before migration if reliable data is available.
items.because: That would show the operational effect.

items.says: Make clear whether you led or contributed to the migration.
Substantiate or remove the broad adoption and impact claims.
items.because: The bullet does not show what changed, how outcomes were measured, or concrete evidence of adoption.

items.says: Define “working context” and explain how the token limit and growth were measured.
items.because: The stress-test setup matters for interpreting the result.

items.says: Clarify the practical reliability or completion impact of removing deadlocks and lost results, if measured.
Give context for “50-way fan-out.”
items.because: Readers may be unfamiliar with the system.

items.says: Clarify what the eight metrics assess.
Clarify your contribution and the scope or use of the metrics integration.
items.because: The count alone does not fully communicate the work.

items.says: Explain what the evaluator’s score was correlated with.
items.because: Without that reference, the 0.89 figure is hard to interpret.

items.says: Explain what the 400+ trials represent.
The backlog result and sensor-signal scale duplicate the internship bullet.
items.because: The result belongs in the section that represents the work unless this was a genuinely separate system and outcome.

items.says: Git is listed as a programming language.
items.because: It is a version-control tool.

items.says: The ML & Agents list is very short relative to your experience.
items.because: Additional relevant tools you have used could better represent it.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific.
items.because: The broad term is less helpful for keyword screening.
